subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Apollo Moon Landings
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Apollo Moon Landings.

hook.text: Between 1969 and 1972, twelve humans walked on the Moon. They brought back 382 kg of rocks that transformed lunar science.

buildup.text: Apollo 11 was the first landing. Neil Armstrong's 'one small step' was watched by 600 million people worldwide.

discovery.text: Apollo samples proved the Moon formed from a giant impact. They also revealed the Moon's volcanic past and true age.

twist.text: Apollo 17 geologist Harrison Schmitt found orange soil—tiny glass beads from an ancient volcanic eruption 3.7 billion years ago.

climax.text: No human has returned since 1972. Artemis aims to change that—landing the first woman and first person of color on the Moon.

punchline.text: Twelve people, six landings, 382 kg of Moon rocks. The greatest exploration feat so far.

quiz.question: What did Apollo moon rocks reveal about the Moon's origin?
options: They proved the Moon formed from a giant impact with early Earth
They showed the Moon captured water from passing comets
They confirmed the Moon was once part of Mars

details.summary: Between 1969 and 1972, NASA's Apollo program landed twelve astronauts on the Moon across six missions. They collected 382 kg of lunar samples, deployed scientific instruments, and took iconic photographs.
details.whyItMatters: Apollo proved humans can explore other worlds. The lunar samples revolutionized our understanding of the Moon's origin, age, and composition. The program inspired generations and demonstrated the potential of human spaceflight.
takeaways: Six missions landed twelve astronauts on the Moon (1969-1972)
Returned 382 kg of lunar samples to Earth
Humanity's only crewed exploration beyond low Earth orbit

faq.question: What did we learn from Apollo lunar samples?
faq.answer: Samples confirmed the Giant Impact origin of the Moon, showed the Moon is ancient (4.5 billion years old), revealed its volcanic history through basaltic mare samples, and proved it formed hot (magma ocean theory).

faq.question: Why haven't humans returned to the Moon since 1972?
faq.answer: After achieving the geopolitical goal of beating the Soviets, political will and funding evaporated. Apollo was extremely expensive (~$25 billion in 1970s dollars). NASA's budget was redirected to the Space Shuttle and ISS.
